title: Benjamini–Tzalik Conjecture on connectivity and reconstructibility
statement_text: There exists a connectivity threshold $k_0$ such that every $k_0$-connected graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}$ has its full vertex set reconstructible from the edge lengths.
context_text: It is folklore that a graph is globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if it is 2-connected. Benjamini and Tzalik conjectured an analogous connectivity condition would guarantee reconstructibility for arbitrary point sets in $\mathbb{R}$. The current paper disproves this via Theorem 1.5.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture via Theorem 1.5: for every positive integer $k$, there exist $k$-connected graphs on arbitrarily many vertices embeddable in the real line such that the largest reconstructible subset of vertices has size exactly $k$.

title: Informal conjecture on sharp threshold for linear-proportion reconstruction
statement_text: Let $V$ be a set of $n$ points on the real line, and suppose the graph of known pairwise distances $(V,\mathcal{P})$ is distributed as $\mathcal{G}(n,(1+\varepsilon)/n)$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is a constant. Then with high probability there is a reconstructible set of size $\Omega_\varepsilon(n)$; that is, the correct threshold for the existence of a reconstructible set of size $\Omega(n)$ is $p=(1+\varepsilon)/n$.
context_text: Let $V\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a set of $n$ labelled points, and suppose that only the distances $|u-v|$ for pairs $uv$ in a set $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\binom{V}{2}$ are known, where $(V,\mathcal{P})$ is the binomial random graph $\mathcal{G}(n,p)$ (each distance is revealed independently with probability $p$); the point set itself is arbitrary. A set $U\subseteq V$ is reconstructible if the positions of its points can be deduced up to isometry, equivalently all pairwise distances within $U$ can be deduced from the known ones; whp means with probability tending to 1. Benjamini and Tzalik showed that $V$ is whp fully reconstructible when $p=C\log n/n$ for a large constant $C$. The authors prove that whp there is a reconstructible set of size $\Omega(n)$ if $p\ge 42/n$, and of size $(1-o(1))n$ if $pn\to\infty$, with a sharp hitting-time result for full reconstruction. Since for $p=c/n$ with $c<1$ all components have size $O(\log n)$, $1/n$ is a weak threshold for a linear-size reconstructible set; the authors conjecture a sharp threshold at $1/n$, where the giant component of $\mathcal{G}(n,p)$ appears. Their approach (via cycles of length at most $0.9\log n$) cannot give a constant better than $9$, and bootstrapping would not reach $(1+\varepsilon)/n$, since most pairs are then only in cycles of length $\Omega(\log(n)/\varepsilon)$.
notes: Appears in footnote 2 as an informal belief. Section 4 (open problems) is not present in the extracted text, so additional conjectures from that section may be missing.
